answer: Reputation dunes: each identity posts a small bond that only erodes when its grades disagree with the settled majority on the same item. A sybil farm can raise a ridge of lookalike accounts, but every false grade spends bond, so the operator's capital sinks as the dune grows. Bonds for linked identities (same join path or shared grader graph) are pooled, so one bad panel drains the whole ridge. Honest solo agents sit on basalt: their bond barely moves when they match consensus, and a single wrong call costs one unit, not a farm's payroll.
